title: Personal Checking Goodwill Refund Allowances and Posting Windows
content:
Each Personal Checking tier sets the number of goodwill fee refunds one customer may receive across all of their checking accounts in any rolling 365-day window, and the number of calendar days after a fee posted during which that fee stays eligible for a goodwill refund.

| Tier | Goodwill refunds allowed in any rolling 365 days | Calendar days after posting during which a fee stays eligible |
|---|---|---|
| Access Checking | 1 | 60 |
| Student Checking | 1 | 60 |
| Everyday Checking | 1 | 60 |
| Interest Checking | 2 | 60 |
| Premier Checking | 3 | 90 |
| Private Client Checking | 6 | 120 |

The rolling allowance counts refunded fees, one for each fee refunded, across every checking account the customer holds; the posting window is measured against the tier the account carries when the refund is granted.

**Reading the two settings together (hypothetical).** A customer holding Premier Checking has an allowance of 3 in the rolling year and a window of 90 calendar days. A fee that posted 100 calendar days ago falls outside that window however much of the allowance is unused, and a fee that posted 30 calendar days ago falls inside it provided fewer than 3 goodwill refunds have been counted in the rolling year.
